head_commit.message:
Merge write-lock/supervision-plane reconciliation

Resolves a 4-way independently-built collision in safety-critical lease/
process-supervision code (main checkout's own fix, control/writer-lock-
semantic-diff-20261006, integration/process-supervision-closure-20261006,
plus an untracked 4th variant sitting in the main checkout). OpenCode
delegated work, independently reviewed before merge (not taken on word):

- Adopts ultimate_pipeline/governance/single_writer/ wholesale from
  control/writer-lock-semantic-diff-20261006 (the only variant actually
  wired into a real call path, now confirmed to be tools/supervised_ue_run.py
  specifically -- an earlier comparison report's claim that it was wired into
  main_pipeline.py was independently checked and found false, corrected here).
  Windows named mutex authority, PID+creation-time identity, explicit
  non-auto-reclaim, Job Object supervision with lease-job coupling.
- Cherry-picks the C11 reproducibility guards (inputs_manifest.py,
  proj_env_guard.py) from integration/process-supervision-closure-20261006,
  pure renames into governance/reproducibility/ (confirmed zero content diff
  via git's own rename detection), 12 callers updated.
- Keeps exactly one copy of the T6 validation harness, discards the main
  checkout's own untracked 4th variant entirely (confirmed zero production
  importers of the discarded copy).
- Carries forward the real lease-wiring bugfix from
  fix/harness-identity-contract-20261006: release(lease, terminal_state) and
  lease_owner_alive() were defined but never called by the harness -- now
  wired into supervised_ue_run.py, preflight.py, heartbeat(), is_stale(),
  reconcile_stale(), and ungoverned_detector.py.

Independently re-verified end to end, twice: once via a disposable detached
worktree (129/0 failed across 3 focused batches), once by a separate
independent reviewer against the pushed tip (+64 collected/+64 passed/0
failed/0 errors versus the real e4f7a45a base; the sole suite-wide failure,
test_no_hardcoded_username_in_production_defaults, confirmed to reproduce
identically on the untouched baseline -- not introduced by this work).
Reviewer verdict: no defects found across provenance byte-identity, rename
completeness, scope containment, and isolation from main_pipeline.py/
writer_lock.py.

head_commit.message:
fix(rq3): Grid0828-only governed manual reference + fix a real duplicate-kwarg bug

Cherry-picked 0e92f053 ("map pair authority with SHA-based identity,
Grid0828 only manual reference") onto current production, now that its
real dependency (the NEW-316..333 perception/environment package) is
merged. This commit was sitting on a separate, divergent line of history
and could not be merged until that dependency landed.

Deliberately NOT a revert: this narrowing is the correct, intentional
direction. is_ingolstadt_auto_arm() now requires the pinned
auto_map_of_record SHA to match (path-based heuristics removed entirely);
INGOLSTADT_MANUAL_COOKED_TOWNS is reduced to Grid0828 only because Grid0828
is the only manual reference with real governed identity fields (source
XODR SHA, cooked package SHA, runtime identity SHA) -- Grid0821 was never
given that same treatment, so excluding it is fail-closed, not a regression.
experiment_map_pair_authority.py becomes the single authority for
Ingolstadt pair validation.

Found and fixed a real bug in the cherry-picked code before committing:
experiment_map_pair_authority.py's build_pair_manifest() call had an entire
block of ~14 keyword arguments duplicated verbatim (and 6 of those tripled),
causing `SyntaxError: keyword argument repeated: manual_map_identity` --
this file could not even be imported as committed upstream. Removed the
duplicates, keeping exactly one of each (verified against
build_pair_manifest()'s real keyword-only signature in
rq3_capture_contract.py).

Also includes the 2 test updates (test_ingolstadt_manual_and_auto_arms,
test_case10_town10hd_control_cannot_be_paired_ingolstadt_capture) that were
never synced to this narrowing: both now use Grid0828 as the valid manual
arm, assert Grid0821 is correctly REJECTED (not just removed from the
fixture), and use the real pinned auto_map_of_record SHA instead of a dummy
placeholder.

Verified: 25/25 in test_rq3_paired_capture_contract.py; 57/57 in
test_perception_environment_hardening_new316_333.py (confirms the
dependency merge didn't regress). Full bare suite follows separately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
fix(carla_tools): extend structural_fingerprint to v2 + fix missing OSM_FILE fallback

Two independently-verified fixes, bundled together since both came out of
today's backlog triage and both touch no overlapping code:

1. structural_fingerprint() (map_runtime_identity.py) previously hashed only
   {x,y,z,h,p,r,length} per road geometry segment and {id,type,connection_count}
   per junction -- an unprompted audit (NEW-350..374) claimed this let two
   structurally different maps sharing road/junction IDs produce identical
   digests. Independently confirmed real via a throwaway adversarial test:
   4/4 constructed collisions (arc-vs-line, curvature 0.01 vs 0.05, differing
   spiral/paramPoly3 coefficients, differing junction contactPoint) all
   produced the SAME digest before this fix. Now captures geometry type per
   segment, the relevant curvature/polynomial coefficients (quantized to 6
   places), and full sorted junction connection topology (incomingRoad/
   connectingRoad/contactPoint/laneLinks), not just connection_count. Schema
   bumped to map_structural_fingerprint_v2. No persisted v1 fingerprints
   exist anywhere (all consumers compute at runtime) and no hardcoded v1
   digest is compared anywhere, so this is a safe, non-breaking extension.
   6 new permanent regression tests pin the fix; all 4 original collisions
   now produce distinct digests. 61/61 passing in the affected test file.

2. OSM_FILE's default (cities/ingolstadt/osm/ingolstadt.osm) doesn't exist on
   this machine, and the existing _pick_existing() fallback chain only tried
   that same non-existent path -- causing every RQ1 trial run to fail at the
   DEM stage with osm_source_unavailable. Added the real authoritative file
   (campaigns/ingolstadt_cooked_perception_v1/source/ingolstadt_authoritative.osm,
   11MB, already present in this repo) as a fallback. Verified: OSM_FILE now
   resolves to that file and the path exists; verify_crs_contract() returns
   real OSM bounds instead of osm_source_unavailable; all 16 DEM F1 tests and
   13 OSM2World wiring tests still pass; the rq1b driver's explicit
   UP_OSM_FILE override is unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
Merge RQ1 determinism-matrix correction: honest INCOMPLETE (0/5 admissible runs)

OpenCode delegated work, self-corrected after I flagged a concrete anomaly
(stage-03/05 identical sha256+mtime in the prior run_00 receipt) and a
confused rationalization ("FAIL demonstrates hardening is working" -- wrong
reasoning for a determinism check). Root-caused for real, not explained away:

- The stage-03/05 duplicate is genuine code behavior, not fabrication or a
  hash-cache bug: stage_05_geometry.py passes topo_fixed into a function
  whose parameter is misleadingly named elev_out (no 04_elevation artifact
  exists yet at that point); under THESIS_STRICT=true, stage 6 takes a
  read-only diagnostic path that writes via shutil.copy2, which preserves
  mtime -- exactly explaining the identical hash+mtime. Confirmed on disk
  (04:58:55 vs 05:20:58 creation times, same 138932131-byte content).
- Separately found: the ORIGINAL run_00_receipt.json (merged 2026-09-30,
  previously treated as verified) claims stage 06 == stage 03, which no real
  run actually produces (a real freeze yields a different byte count) --
  its own driver admits that receipt came from undocumented, uncommitted
  "additional post-processing." That earlier "verified" status should be
  treated as unreliable, not re-confirmed.
- The prior FAIL verdict was not real measured nondeterminism -- three real
  harness bugs caused it: output_path was compared as if it should match
  across isolated run directories (impossible by construction); a
  structural_signature metric mismatch conflated junction elements with
  roads-carrying-a-junction-ref; the matrix builder ignored each receipt's
  own status field entirely.
- Real result once harness bugs were fixed: structural signature is
  identical across run_01-04 (32266 roads / 22588 junctions /
  1487573.69m) wherever they ran -- but all 4 runs failed at the DEM stage
  with osm_source_unavailable (OSM_FILE points at a file that does not
  exist on this machine). Honest verdict: INCOMPLETE, 0 of 5 admissible
  runs -- not a pass, not evidence of either determinism or nondeterminism.

Tests: 18/18 for the RQ1-specific suite (was 4); broader unit run 2507
passed/1 failed, with that 1 failure independently confirmed to reproduce on
a pristine baseline checkout (pre-existing, unrelated).

NOT addressed by this merge: the missing OSM_FILE itself (a real, separate
environment-configuration gap blocking any further RQ1 trial), and the ~20
other branches/worktrees that accumulated on this repo between 2026-10-02
and 2026-10-06, none of which have reached this production branch and none
of which are touched by this merge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
test(process-control): publish supervision acceptance suite, fix spawn handle leak

Adds the two producers behind the 25/25 matrix and 270/270 stress claims so
they are re-runnable from a clean checkout instead of being receipt-backed
only. Both were audited and needed no portability change: they derive REPO
from __file__, isolate fixtures with tempfile.mkdtemp, and write evidence
only to reports/.

Fixing the handle metric they exposed:

test_job_stress.py measured handles via GetProcessMemoryInfo with a
hand-rolled PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS that declared handles and threads
fields, which do not exist in the real structure, and it set cb to its own
wrong size. The call therefore failed and returned 0, so every before/after
pair read 0 -> 0 and the leak check passed vacuously. Replaced with
GetProcessHandleCount, and an invalid (now zero) reading is treated as a
failure rather than as no growth.

With a working metric the stress suite showed +56 handles, and isolating the
two phases showed the growth was strictly linear at one handle per spawn:
JobSupervisor.close() released only the job handle and never the hProcess
handles handed out by spawn(), so every child leaked one handle for the
lifetime of the process tree. The Job create/close path spawns nothing,
which is why the earlier create/close-only measurement read delta 0 and did
not catch it.

_OwnedProcess now releases its hProcess as soon as the exit code is
observed and caches that code, so poll() keeps its Popen-compatible
behaviour; kill() on an already-terminated child is a no-op rather than an
error. Supervisor.close() releases only children that have already
terminated, so callers may still poll or wait a child after closing.

Post-fix, per-batch deltas for the spawn/terminate path are 2, 0, 0 with
zero idle drift, i.e. bounded rather than linear.

Measured in this worktree: matrix 25/25; stress 270/270 with handles
176 -> 181 (growth 5, measurement valid); T6 5/5 across setup, owner death,
reconciliation and reacquire; lease/job coupling 11/11 with coupling T7
handles 184 -> 184 delta 0; 15/15 identity and API-contract tests; 0 native
crashes.

head_commit.message:
fix(process-control): bind lease owner identity to owner-published authority

T6 asserted lease.root_pid == hp.pid. On Windows a venv
Scripts\python.exe is a redirector that forks the real interpreter, so
Popen's PID is the launcher while the lease owner is its child. The
assertion therefore failed against a correct lease.

Measured in reports/T6_PROCESS_LAUNCH_TOPOLOGY.json: owner PID 37056 has
OS parent PID 21980 == the launcher PID, with executables
.venv\Scripts\python.exe vs ...\Python312\python.exe.

Identity authority is now the owner-published record
(authority.owner_pid / owner_creation_time). hp.pid is retained only as
launch-topology evidence, and owner authority is verified to belong to the
launched hierarchy before the gate proceeds.

Four further defects surfaced once the gate became honest:

- lease_job_coupling.py passed repo_sha to SingleWriterLease.acquire(),
  which takes no OperationLease metadata. The holder died with TypeError
  before creating its Job, cascading T6a/T6b/T6c.
- lease_job_coupling.py asserted a nonexistent lease.owner_identity key,
  and killed the launcher instead of the logical owner, so the lease read
  LIVE and reconciliation correctly refused.
- t6_determinism.py also killed the launcher, so owner death was never
  actually exercised. It now kills the logical owner and asserts its death.
- A WinError 5 flake on stage.json os.replace: Python's open() does not
  grant FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so a concurrent reader made the atomic replace
  fail. Replaced with a bounded retry.

The coupling suite also asserted a stale lease was denied before
reconciliation, but acquire() deliberately reconciles a STALE record inline
while holding the mutex. Corrected to assert the invariants that hold:
reacquire succeeds after reconciliation, and live-lease reconciliation is
denied (REFUSING_TO_RECONCILE_LIVE_LEASE).

Base-interpreter launch was deliberately NOT substituted; the venv launch
path is retained and launcher identity is kept distinct from logical
lease-owner identity.

Hardcoded REPO = r'C:\\Users\\admin\\...' replaced with a __file__-derived
path in all three harnesses, matching the convention already used by the
new unit test, so the harness runs on CI and non-portable paths are not
published.

T6 5/5 across two independent series, coupling 11/11, handles 187 -> 187
(GetProcessHandleCount, delta 0), no native crashes.

head_commit.message:
fix(perception): repair 4 regressions introduced by NEW-271..292 commit

Fixes 4 bugs an independent verification subagent found in commit a6c46055,
each with exact evidence before this fix:

1. local_perception_runner.py: def __init__ had lost its 4-space class-method
   indentation (sat at column 0 right after the class docstring), so the
   whole file failed to parse (IndentationError at the next method def).
   This transitively broke NEW-271's own delivery path (run_perception_capture_pair.py
   imports this class) and the repo's own pre-existing
   test_sys001_import_smoke.py::test_all_root_py_files_compile. One-line fix:
   restore the 4-space indent.

2. perception_metrics.py: the .ply/.bin/.npz LiDAR-detection block (NEW-272/273)
   was dedented outside both camera-scanning loops, so it ran at most once
   using whatever `lower`/`path` were left over from the last camera file --
   or raised UnboundLocalError on an empty/no-camera run
   (test_empty_run_dir_no_sensor_data) -- and never actually counted LiDAR
   frames correctly (test_lidar_bin_files_counted expected 3, got 1). Fixed
   by giving LiDAR detection its own dedicated walk over a sibling lidar/
   directory (matching the test fixtures' own directory layout), with
   per-file loop variables, running independently of which camera branch
   (rgb/ vs. fallback) was taken.

3. run_vision_domain_gap.py: _align_shapes()'s resolution-mismatch error
   message referenced auto_dir/manual_dir/a_path/b_path, none of which are
   in that function's scope (they belong to the caller, run_vision_domain_gap()),
   raising NameError instead of the intended RuntimeError. Fixed by passing
   the real path objects in from the actual call site
   (_compute_pair_metrics, which has auto_path/manual_path) as explicit
   parameters instead of reading them from an enclosing scope that doesn't
   exist for this function.

4. recorder.py: _next_frame_id() raised a bare name, FRAME_ID_MISSING, that
   is never defined anywhere in the repository -- NameError instead of a
   controlled failure on a sensor callback with no valid .frame. Added a
   real FrameIdMissingError(RuntimeError) class with a descriptive message
   and raise an instance of it, preserving the intended fail-closed
   behavior (no fabricated frame IDs) without crashing on an undefined name.

All 4 fixes verified: syntax-valid on all 4 files; the 3 tests an independent
verifier found broken by the original commit
(test_empty_run_dir_no_sensor_data, test_lidar_bin_files_counted,
test_all_root_py_files_compile) now pass, 26/26 in the targeted run. Full
bare pytest run follows separately before this branch is considered for
merge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
